display.purpose: Screen titles only — one per screen, at the top.

headline.purpose: The number that is the point of a card: session totals, stat-tile values.

body.purpose: List-row titles, form values, primary reading text.

label.purpose: Secondary text, subtitles, chips, segment labels, metadata.

label-strong.purpose: Button labels and in-card section headers — same size as Label, separated by weight alone.

code.purpose: Identifiers and raw values; 700 weight on Android.

shadows.name: floating-action
shadows.purpose: The floating action button ONLY. The single shadow in the system; every other surface is flat and separates by tone.

motion.name: press-feedback
motion.purpose: The universal touch response for buttons, rows and FAB. No hover states — this is a touch platform.

breakpoints.name: max-content
breakpoints.purpose: Content column cap (MaxContentWidth) so list rows stay readable on tablets.

breakpoints.name: bottom-tab-inset-ios
breakpoints.purpose: Scroll-content padding clearing the tab bar on iOS.

breakpoints.name: bottom-tab-inset-android
breakpoints.purpose: Scroll-content padding clearing the tab bar on Android.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single most important action on a screen. Full width, one per screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #B98CFF; color: #1A1226; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 20px; padding: 16px 24px; width: 100%; border: none; border-radius: 12px; transition: opacity 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:active { opacity: 0.85; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F6EEE4; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The base raised surface for tiles, list groups and forms. Flat — never shadowed.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #221934; color: #F6EEE4; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; } .ds-card-label { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 20px; color: #C9B9DC; } .ds-card-value { font-size: 32px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 44px; }

components.name: Stat Tile
components.description: A big number above its caption — Home's header totals and every stats readout.
components.css: .ds-stat-tile { background: #221934; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 2px; } .ds-stat-value { color: #F6EEE4; font-size: 32px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 36px; } .ds-stat-label { color: #C9B9DC; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 20px; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Chip (neutral)
components.description: Small pill label — session type, tags, discipline.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: #2E2246; color: #F6EEE4; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 20px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; }

components.name: Chip (primary)
components.description: Reserved for a genuine achievement or an active filter — never general labelling.
components.css: .ds-chip-primary { display: inline-block; background: #B98CFF; color: #1A1226; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 20px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: The app's signature selector. Labels never wrap; past four options it scrolls instead of squeezing.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: flex; gap: 2px; padding: 2px; background: #221934; border-radius: 12px; } .ds-seg-item { flex: 1; padding: 8px; border: none; background: transparent; color: #C9B9DC; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 20px; border-radius: 8px; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; } .ds-seg-item--on { background: #2E2246; color: #F6EEE4; } .ds-seg-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #B98CFF; outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: List Row
components.description: One row in a list group — session, firearm or settings entry. Separated by tone, not dividers.
components.html: Träning Precision3 Sept 2026 · 251p · ⌀ 41.8 · 1XTraining
components.css: .ds-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 8px 0; gap: 8px; } .ds-row-text { display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .ds-row-title { color: #F6EEE4; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px; } .ds-row-sub { color: #C9B9DC; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 20px; } .ds-row:active { opacity: 0.85; }

components.name: Floating Action Button
components.description: Bottom-right, above the tab bar. The only element in the system that casts a shadow.
components.css: .ds-fab { position: absolute; right: 16px; bottom: 16px; background: #B98CFF; color: #1A1226; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 20px; padding: 16px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); cursor: pointer; } .ds-fab:active { opacity: 0.85; }

components.name: Empty State
components.description: Never a bare 'no results' line — a title, an explanation, and the action that would fill the screen.

narrative.overview:
ShotLedger is the notebook a shooter keeps at the range, built to the tolerances of a measuring instrument. A paper logbook is unadorned because its job is to hold numbers accurately and be readable in whatever light the range has; a scoring gauge is exact because a tenth of a millimetre decides a ring. This system answers to both. Every surface exists to report a value, and anything that does not help a number read is removed.

The app is dark by default and near-monochrome by discipline. The ground is a deep ink purple (#16101F), not black, and every neutral above it is purple-tinted rather than grey. Depth comes from tone, not from shadow: surfaces separate by getting lighter, and the only shadow in the entire application belongs to the floating action button. A single lavender accent carries every interactive affordance, and its scarcity is what makes it readable at a glance between series.

Restraint here is functional, not stylistic. The app is used outdoors in bright sunlight, where glare eats low-contrast detail, and it is used in the seconds between shooting one series and starting the next. Contrast is asserted in tests, not eyeballed. Ornament would cost legibility and buy nothing.
keyCharacteristics: Dark ground, purple-tinted neutrals, never grey
Depth by tonal layering; exactly one shadow in the system
One accent, used sparingly, carrying all interaction
A four-step radius scale and a seven-step spacing scale — no ad-hoc values
Contrast treated as a tested invariant, because the range is sunlit
Precise and restrained: tight spacing, sharp hierarchy, no decoration

rules.name: The Purple-Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: There is no grey in the dark theme. Text, secondary text, borders, and every surface carry purple. A neutral grey introduced anywhere reads instantly as foreign and is a defect, not a variation.

rules.name: The Scarce Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Lavender marks interaction and nothing else. It is never decorative, never a heading color, never a background for content. If two lavender elements compete on one screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Rejected Gold Rule
rules.body: A gold accent (#E8B84B) was designed, passed contrast, and was rejected by the maintainer for interactive use. It survives in tokens.ts as PURPLE_RAIN_GOLD_ACCENT_REJECTED so the contrast work is not lost. Never assign it to primary or any other interactive token.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Label and Label Strong are the same 14px; the only difference is weight. Emphasis at small sizes is a weight change, never a size bump, which keeps line rhythm intact in dense rows.

rules.name: The Single-Line Control Rule
rules.body: Control labels never wrap. Segmented-control labels are single-line and shrink or scroll rather than breaking; a label that splits mid-word is a layout defect. Past four options a segmented control scrolls horizontally instead of squeezing every label.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: The floating action button is the only element in ShotLedger permitted a shadow. Cards, tiles, sheets, headers, and chips are flat and separate by tone. Adding a shadow to a card is a defect, not a refinement — it breaks the one signal that means 'this floats'.

rules.name: The One Primary Action Rule
rules.body: PrimaryButton is the single most important action on a screen. A screen with three of them has no primary action.

dos: Do express depth with the tonal stack — Ink Purple → Surface Purple → Raised Surface Purple.
Do take spacing from the seven-step scale (2/4/8/16/24/32/64) and radius from the four-step scale (8/12/20/999).
Do keep Signal Lavender scarce; one interactive accent per screen region.
Do assert contrast in app/src/theme/tokens.test.ts when adding or changing a color — sunlight legibility is a tested invariant here, not a judgement call.
Do keep control labels on one line, shrinking or scrolling instead of wrapping.
Do use weight, not size, to emphasise at 14px.
donts: Don't add a shadow to anything but the floating action button.
Don't introduce a neutral grey into the dark theme; every neutral is purple-tinted.
Don't assign PURPLE_RAIN_GOLD_ACCENT_REJECTED (#E8B84B) to primary or any interactive token — it is retained for its contrast work only.
Don't put more than one Primary Button on a screen.
Don't invent a radius or spacing value outside the scales.
Don't load a custom typeface; the platform system font is the deliberate choice.
Don't let a tab or control label truncate — shorten the string instead.
